statements.claim: Kamsa is the son of King Ugrasena of Mathura
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 'ugrasena-sutaḥ kaṃsaḥ'

statements.claim: Kamsa personally drove the wedding chariot, taking the reins himself
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 'pathi pragrahiṇaṃ kaṃsam'; index summary 'Kamsa drives the chariot'

statements.claim: Devaki was Kamsa's (youngest) sister whom he loved
statements.evidence: HV 1.56 'youngest sister Devaki'; BP 10.1 'svasuḥ priya-cikīrṣayā' (to please his sister)

statements.claim: Four hundred elephants with golden garlands formed the procession
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 'catuḥ-śataṃ ... gajānāṃ hema-mālinām'

statements.claim: Two hundred well-adorned maidservants walked alongside
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 'dāsīnāṃ sukumārīṇāṃ dve śate samalaṅkṛte'

statements.claim: Conches, horns, mridanga drums and kettledrums sounded together
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 'śaṅkha-tūrya-mṛdaṅgāś ca nedur dundubhayaḥ'

statements.claim: Vasudeva the groom sat beside the bride
statements.evidence: Index summary 'newly-wed Vasudeva and Devaki'

statements.claim: A bodiless voice addressed Kamsa
statements.evidence: BP 10.1 'āśarīra-vāk'; VP 5.1 'a voice in the sky ... addressed Kansa'

statements.claim: The voice was deep as thunder and called Kamsa a fool
statements.evidence: VP 5.1 'sounding aloud and deep as thunder ... Fool that you are'

statements.claim: The warning: the woman he drove would bear eight children and the eighth would take his life
statements.evidence: VP 5.1 'the eighth child of the damsel whom you are driving ... shall take away your life'; BP/HV concur

statements.claim: Kamsa drew his sword and turned to kill Devaki in the chariot
statements.evidence: VP 5.1 'Kansa drew his sword, and was about to put Devakí to death'

statements.claim: Vasudeva interposed, stepping between the blade and the bride
statements.evidence: VP 5.1 'but Vasudeva interposed'

statements.claim: Only Kamsa heard the voice; the music played on and the procession halted
statements.evidence: Atmosphere/framing not asserted in the pack (no sourceable fact)

statements.claim: Closing reflection on affection turning to dread and every future child being watched
statements.evidence: Non-factual reflective narration; consistent with the prophecy premise

notes: Faithful to BP/VP bodiless-voice variant; Harivamsha's Narada variant is correctly deferred to the tradition_note, so no contradiction.

statements.claim: The birth occurred at midnight
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'niśīthe ... jāyamāne janārdane'

statements.claim: The directions grew calm, the sky cleared, and the stars rose
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'diśaḥ prasedur gaganaṃ nirmaloḍu-gaṇodayam'

statements.claim: Rivers settled clear and ponds put on lotus flowers
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'nadyaḥ prasanna-salilā hradā jalaruha-śriyaḥ'

statements.claim: The seas took up a low melodious murmur
statements.evidence: VP 5.3 'the seas with their own melodious murmurings made the music'

statements.claim: A gentle, cool, sweet-scented wind rose
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'vavau vāyuḥ sukha-sparśaḥ puṇya-gandhavahaḥ śuciḥ'

statements.claim: Extinguished hearth-fires burned again with a mild gentle flame
statements.evidence: HV 1.59 'the fires, that had been extinguished, began to burn'; VP 5.3 'the holy fires glowed with a mild and gentle flame'

statements.claim: A soft light spread over the earth like poured moonlight
statements.evidence: VP 5.3 'as if moonlight was diffused over the whole earth'

statements.claim: The minds of good people grew suddenly at peace
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'manāṃsy āsan prasannāni sādhūnām'

statements.claim: Devaki and Vasudeva were shut away by Kamsa, who had killed her earlier children by dashing them
statements.evidence: HV 1.59 'Kansa killed the Sargarbhas by dashing them against a stone'; prison setting in title/summary

statements.claim: The night was called Jayanti, the star Abhijit, the moment Vijaya
statements.evidence: HV 1.59 'the night was Jayanti, the Nakshatra was Abhijit and Muhurtta was Vijaya'

statements.claim: Kinnaras and gandharvas sang; siddhas and charanas praised
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'jaguḥ kinnara-gandharvās tuṣṭuvuḥ siddha-cāraṇāḥ'

statements.claim: Sages and gods showered flowers; a celestial bugle sounded unstruck
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'mumucur munayo devāḥ sumanāṃsi'; HV 1.59 'celestial bugles began to produce sound without being struck'

statements.claim: 'Almost no one noticed'; the city slept while nature rejoiced
statements.evidence: Connective framing around the sourced natural-portent verses; not itself a factual claim

notes: Nature-portent sequence maps directly onto BP 10.3.1-7 and HV 1.59. The four-armed reveal is correctly deferred to tradition_note (VP 5.3), so no omission is treated as an error.

statements.claim: News of the birth tore Kamsa from sleep at night
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 'sa talpāt tūrṇam utthāya' (rose swiftly from his bed)

statements.claim: The guards told him a daughter had been born in the prison
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 'te tu tūrṇam upavrajya devakyā garbha-janma tat'; summary 'the infant girl'

statements.claim: He rose agitated, certain this was the dreaded moment
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 'kālo 'yam iti vihvalaḥ' ('This is the time,' he thought, agitated)

statements.claim: He rushed to the prison/lying-in room
statements.evidence: Index summary 'hastens to the lying-in room'

statements.claim: Devaki is Kamsa's own younger sister
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 'avarajā'

statements.claim: Kamsa had killed her earlier children
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 'bahavo hiṃsitā bhrātaḥ śiśavaḥ'

statements.claim: Devaki called the lost children 'bright as fire'
statements.evidence: BP 10.4 'pāvakopamāḥ' (resembling fire)

statements.claim: Devaki pleaded with him to spare the infant girl
statements.evidence: Index summary 'the grieving Devaki begs him to spare the infant girl'

statements.claim: Kamsa tore the child from her hands and raised her up
statements.evidence: Index summary 'tears the child from her hands'; content_note 'raises it to dash it'

statements.claim: Palace/lamplight atmosphere and 'fear is older than mercy' aside
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing; no sourceable claim

statements.claim: 'What he meant to do next belongs to the moment that follows'
statements.evidence: Deliberate deferral to the next story; not a factual assertion

notes: Devaki's plea closely tracks BP 10.4.1-6 Sanskrit ('children like fire', 'your younger sister', 'sons slain'). No invented characters or events.

statements.claim: Vasudeva was prompted by the Lord (a quiet command) to carry the child out
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'bhagavat-pracoditaḥ' (prompted by the Lord)

statements.claim: He carried the baby from the lying-in room at night
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'sūtikā-gṛhāt'

statements.claim: The guards were struck by sleep (the goddess of sleep/Yogamaya)
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'hṛta-pratyaya-sarva-vṛttiṣu dvāḥ-stheṣu'; VP 5.3 'guards all charmed by Yoganidrá'

statements.claim: The prison doors opened by themselves, as darkness gives way before the sun
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'svayaṃ vyavaryanta yathā tamo raveḥ'

statements.claim: A heavy rain fell from the clouds of night
statements.evidence: VP 5.3 'heavy rain that fell from the clouds of night'; BP 10.3 'maghoni varṣaty'

statements.claim: Shesha the many-headed serpent spread his hoods above them as shelter
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 / VP 5.3 'spread his hoods above their heads'

statements.claim: The Yamuna was deep, swift and foaming in flood
statements.evidence: BP 10.3 'gambhīra-toyaugha-javormi-phenilā'

statements.claim: The Yamuna parted; waters rose no higher than his knee
statements.evidence: VP 5.3 'the waters were stilled, and rose not above his knee'; BP summary 'parts its waters'

statements.claim: He carried the child on toward Gokul, the cowherd settlement
statements.evidence: Index summary/arc 'krishna_reaches_gokul'; location Gokula

statements.claim: 'The child was only a few hours old', 'the river knew what it carried', 'no one knew anything had happened'
statements.evidence: Connective framing; consistent with same-night escape, not independent factual claims

notes: Lock/sleep/serpent/river miracles all grounded in BP 10.3.46-49 and VP 5.3. No unsupported or contradicted elements.

statements.claim: Putana was a child-killer demoness who came by night
statements.evidence: VP 5.5 'Pútaná, the child-killer, came thither by night'; BP 10.6 'bālaka-mārikā'

statements.claim: She moved from house to house searching for children
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'vicinvatī śiśūn' (searching for children)

statements.claim: By chance she reached Nanda's house
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'yadṛcchayā nanda-gṛhe'

statements.claim: She took up the sleeping infant and gave him her breast
statements.evidence: VP 5.5 'took him up, and gave him her breast to suck'

statements.claim: The breast held poison meant to kill the child
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.22 'breast of deadly poison'; BP 10.6 'stanaṃ durjara-vīryam'

statements.claim: The baby's eyes stayed closed; he drank without waking or crying
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'sa nimīlitekṣaṇaḥ' (with closed eyes)

statements.claim: Krishna drained out her life along with her milk
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'drinks out her life along with her milk'; VP 5.5 'drained it of the life'

statements.claim: She cried 'Let go, let go'
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'sā muñca muñcālam iti prabhāṣiṇī'

statements.claim: Her cry shook the earth, mountains, sky and the planets
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'sādrir mahī dyauś ca cacāla sa-grahā'

statements.claim: She fell in her monstrous true form, hair loose and limbs spread, like Vritra struck by a thunderbolt
statements.evidence: BP 10.6 'vyādāya keśāṃś caraṇau bhujāv api prasārya ... nija-rūpam ... vajrāhato vṛtra ivāpatan'

statements.claim: Uddhava later recalled Putana attained a nurse's place despite her murderous intent
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.22 'attained the goal of a nurse' (Uddhava's recollection)

statements.claim: Household woke and found them; by daylight they carried the body away
statements.evidence: Scene-closing connective; body disposal not within excerpted BP 10.6.6-12 but consistent with the episode's canonical continuation

notes: All substantive claims trace to BP 10.6.6-12, BP 3.2.22, HV 1.61 and VP 5.5. The body-removal closing is treated as connective (it is canonically accurate but outside the excerpted verse range).

statements.claim: Trinavarta came as a whirlwind and snatched the baby
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'tṛṇāvartaḥ ... vātyā-rūpa-dharo haran' (whirlwind-form, carrying)

statements.claim: The child grew heavier than a mountain/stone
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'guru-mattayā'; index summary 'heavier than a mountain'

statements.claim: The baby seized him by the throat; he could not move or breathe and his eyes bulged
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'gala-grahaṇa-niśceṣṭo daityo nirgata-locanaḥ'

statements.claim: He fell from the sky onto a rock and was shattered
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'antarikṣāt patitaṃ śilāyāṃ viśīrṇa-sarvāvayavaṃ'

statements.claim: The cowherds found the child safe on the demon's chest
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'kṛṣṇaṃ ca tasyorasi lambamānam'; index summary

statements.claim: The mothers recovered the child unmarked and wept with relief
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'prādāya mātre pratihṛtya vismitāḥ' (returned to the mother, amazed)

statements.claim: The people asked 'What penance have we done, what worship, what good deeds, what kindness to other beings'
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'kiṃ nas tapaś cīrṇam adhokṣajārcanaṃ pūrteṣṭa-dattam uta bhūta-sauhṛdam'

statements.claim: Nanda saw many wonders in the broad forest and began to watch the child more closely
statements.evidence: BP 10.7 'dṛṣṭvādbhutāni bahuśo nanda-gopo bṛhadvane'

statements.claim: Dust/darkness atmosphere, 'a child is the lightest thing in the world', women at their churning
statements.evidence: Non-factual connective framing; no sourceable claims

notes: Every plot beat maps to BP 10.7.25-32. No invented events, characters or numbers.

statements.claim: Garga performed the naming rites secretly, without the cowherds' knowledge
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 / index summary 'in secret'; VP 5.6 'without the knowledge of the cowherds'

statements.claim: Garga was sent by Vasudeva to perform the rites
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 / VP 5.6 'sent to Gokula by Vasudeva for that purpose'

statements.claim: Kamsa was hunting Vasudeva's children and knew of Nanda's friendship with Vasudeva
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'kaṃsaḥ pāpa-matiḥ sakhyaṃ tava cānakadundubheḥ'

statements.claim: Nanda rose with joy, pressed his palms, seated Garga and offered him a guest's welcome
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'taṃ dṛṣṭvā parama-prītaḥ pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ ... kṛtātithyaṃ sūpaviṣṭaṃ'

statements.claim: Garga read the course of the stars with knowledge beyond the senses
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'jyotiṣām ayanaṃ sākṣād ... jñānam atīndriyam'

statements.claim: Garga warned that word of a public naming would endanger the child, so it must be quiet
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'kaṃsaḥ pāpa-matiḥ ...' + summary 'in secret'

statements.claim: The elder boy, son of Rohini, was named Rama (also Balarama/Balabhadra)
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 / VP 5.6 'son of Rohini named Rama ... Balabhadra'

statements.claim: Nanda's son was named Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 / VP 5.6 'named ... the other Krishna'

statements.claim: The child appears in age after age with a different color
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'āsan varṇās trayo hy asya ... anuyugaṃ tanūḥ'

statements.claim: His names and forms are beyond counting
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca'

statements.claim: Before this birth he was born of Vasudeva
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'prāg ayaṃ vasudevasya ... jātaḥ'

statements.claim: He would bring welfare and delight to the cowherds and all Gokula
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'eṣa vaḥ śreya ādhāsyad gopa-gokula-nandanaḥ'

statements.claim: Through him the good would be shielded from harm
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'purānena ... sādhavo dasyu-pīḍitāḥ'

statements.claim: Those who set their hearts on him are fortunate
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'ya etasmin mahā-bhāgāḥ prītiṃ kurvanti mānavāḥ'

statements.claim: He is equal to Narayana in qualities
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'nārāyaṇa-samo guṇaiḥ'

statements.claim: 'A naming can be a dangerous thing' and the closing reflection on the name spreading worldwide
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing; no sourceable claim

notes: Garga's speech and the two names map line-by-line onto BP 10.8.1-19 and VP 5.6. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna played with Rama and the other cowherd boys
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'rāmādyā gopa-dārakāḥ'

statements.claim: The boys accused Krishna of eating mud in secret
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'kasmān mṛdam ... bhakṣitavān rahaḥ'; index summary 'playmates accuse him of eating mud'

statements.claim: Yasoda took him by the hand and scolded him gently, as a well-wisher
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'sā gṛhītvā kare kṛṣṇam upālabhya hitaiṣiṇī'

statements.claim: Krishna denied it, saying they all accused him falsely
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'nāhaṃ bhakṣitavān amba sarve mithyābhiśaṃsinaḥ'

statements.claim: Yasoda asked him to open his mouth
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'yady evaṃ tarhi vyādehī'

statements.claim: In his mouth she saw the whole universe, moving and unmoving, with sky and directions
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'sā tatra dadṛśe viśvaṃ jagat sthāsnu ca khaṃ diśaḥ'; summary 'mountains, oceans, stars'

statements.claim: She saw the circle of stars, water, fire, air and space
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'jyotiś-cakraṃ jalaṃ tejo nabhasvān viyad eva ca'

statements.claim: She saw every living thing, time, and the tangle of deeds and their results
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'jīva-kāla ... karmāśaya'

statements.claim: The vision sages seek through the Vedas, Upanishads and disciplines of knowledge
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'trayyā copaniṣadbhiś ca sāṅkhya-yogaiś ca sātvataiḥ'

statements.claim: Yasoda wondered if it was a dream, divine illusion, or a delusion of her own mind
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'kiṃ svapna etad uta devamāyā kiṃ vā madīyo bata buddhi-mohaḥ'

statements.claim: She reaffirmed 'I am Yasoda, my husband Nanda, my son; wife of the lord of Vraja, mistress of all his wealth'
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'ahaṃ mamāsau patir eṣa me suto vrajeśvarasyākhila-vittapā satī'

statements.claim: Her memory was then veiled and she lifted her son onto her lap
statements.evidence: BP 10.8 'sadyo naṣṭa-smṛtir gopī sāropyāroham ātmajam'

statements.claim: 'His mouth was small enough to kiss' and the closing reflection on forgetting as mercy
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing; no sourceable claim

notes: The cosmic-mouth vision maps directly onto BP 10.8.31-45, including Yasoda's internal monologue. No unsupported or contradicted claims.
